category: Entity Framework, Curated Data Functions, Databases, Resource System & Devices
description: Advanced use of the Entity framework (properties, implicitly defined and derived entity classes, custom entity stores, prefetching, names and types), relational-database access through RelationalDatabase/DatabaseReference and the DatabaseLink package, document and RDF stores, and the Interpreter/SemanticImport type helpers used for natural-language and form input.

tools.name: EntityProperty
tools.description: EntityProperty[type, "prop"] represents a property of an entity type (optionally with qualifiers such as a date or unit), usable in EntityValue, EntityFunction and Dataset queries; EntityPropertyClass groups related properties and EntityProperties (listed) enumerates them. Explicit EntityProperty objects are needed for qualified properties (e.g. population in a given year).
tools.usage:
EntityProperty["type", "prop"]
EntityProperty["type", "prop", {qualifier -> value}]
EntityValue[entity, EntityProperty["Country", "Population", {"Date" -> DateObject[{2000}]}]]
EntityPropertyClass["type", "class"]

tools.name: EntityClassList
tools.description: Lists the predefined entity classes of a type (e.g. "Country" has "Europe", "G20"...), with EntityValue["type", "Entities"] / "EntityCount" / "Properties" giving the type-level information; EntityTypeName returns the type of an entity, CommonName the human-readable name and CanonicalName the canonical identifier string. These are the introspection functions for exploring curated data.
tools.usage:
EntityClassList["type"]
EntityValue["type", "Entities"]
EntityValue["type", "EntityCount"]
EntityValue["type", "Properties"]
EntityTypeName[entity]
CommonName[entity]
CanonicalName[entity]

tools.name: FilteredEntityClass
tools.description: Defines an implicit entity class by a predicate on properties, evaluated lazily by the entity server (or database): FilteredEntityClass[type, EntityFunction[e, cond]]; SortedEntityClass orders by a property, SampledEntityClass takes a subset, and the same specifications work as EntityClass[type, prop -> value] shortcuts. Combining them pushes filtering to the data source instead of downloading everything.
tools.usage:
FilteredEntityClass["type", EntityFunction[e, cond[e]]]
SortedEntityClass[class, "prop"]
SortedEntityClass[class, "prop" -> "Descending"]
SampledEntityClass[class, n]
EntityClass["type", "prop" -> value]
EntityClass["type", {"prop1" -> TakeLargest[5], "prop2" -> GreaterThan[10]}]

parameters.name: cond
parameters.description: Boolean EntityFunction expression in the entity variable using e["prop"] accessors.

tools.name: EntityFunction
tools.description: EntityFunction[e, body] is a pure function over entities whose body uses e["prop"] to access properties and is compiled to a query that runs server-side (or as SQL against a RelationalDatabase). It is used in FilteredEntityClass, ExtendedEntityClass (computed properties), AggregatedEntityClass and EntityValue with computed properties.
tools.usage:
EntityFunction[e, body]
EntityFunction[{e1, e2}, body]
EntityValue[class, EntityFunction[e, e["Population"]/e["Area"]]]

parameters.name: body
parameters.description: Expression in e["prop"] values using arithmetic, comparisons, StringContainsQ, etc.

tools.name: ExtendedEntityClass
tools.description: Derived entity classes: ExtendedEntityClass adds computed properties (EntityFunction) to a class, AggregatedEntityClass groups entities and computes aggregates (like GROUP BY), CombinedEntityClass joins two classes on a shared property (like SQL JOIN), and UnionedEntityClass / IntersectedEntityClass / ComplementedEntityClass perform set operations. Together with FilteredEntityClass and SortedEntityClass they give a full relational algebra over entities that also compiles to SQL for RelationalDatabase stores.
tools.usage:
ExtendedEntityClass[class, "newprop" -> EntityFunction[e, expr]]
AggregatedEntityClass[class, "aggprop" -> EntityFunction[e, Total[e["prop"]]], "groupprop"]
CombinedEntityClass[class1, class2, "prop"]
CombinedEntityClass[class1, class2, EntityFunction[{a, b}, a["x"] == b["y"]], "Inner" | "Left" | "Right" | "Outer"]
UnionedEntityClass[class1, class2]
IntersectedEntityClass[class1, class2]
ComplementedEntityClass[class1, class2]

parameters.name: class
parameters.description: Entity type, EntityClass or derived class.

tools.name: EntityInstance
tools.description: EntityInstance[entity, quals] represents a specific instance of an entity with qualifiers - a quantity of it (EntityInstance[Entity["Food", "Apple"], Quantity[3, ...]]), a dated version, or a parameter setting - so that properties such as nutrition or historical values are computed for that instance; Dated[entity, date] is the shorthand for a date qualifier and EntityGroup groups several entities into one aggregate entity.
tools.usage:
EntityInstance[entity, {qual -> val}]
EntityInstance[entity, Quantity[n, "unit"]]
Dated[entity, date]
EntityGroup[{e1, e2, ...}]
EntityValue[Dated[Entity["Country", "Germany"], 1950], "Population"]

tools.name: EntityStore
tools.description: Defines a custom entity type from your own data: EntityStore[<|"Type" -> <|"Entities" -> <|"id" -> <|"prop" -> value|>|>, "Properties" -> ...|>|>] or from a RelationalDatabase; EntityRegister makes it available so Entity["Type", "id"], EntityValue, EntityList, FilteredEntityClass and Dataset queries work on your data exactly as on built-in data, EntityUnregister removes it and EntityStores lists registered stores. The standard way to give relational or tabular data the entity interface.
tools.usage:
store = EntityStore[<|"Product" -> <|"Entities" -> <|"p1" -> <|"Name" -> "Bolt", "Price" -> 0.5|>, ...|>|>|>]
store = EntityStore[RelationalDatabase[...]]
store = EntityStore[{"Type" -> <|"Entities" -> dataset|>}]
EntityRegister[store]
EntityUnregister[store]
EntityStores[]
EntityValue["Product", {"Name", "Price"}, "Dataset"]

parameters.name: spec
parameters.description: Association of type -> <|"Entities" -> ..., "Properties" -> ..., "Label" -> ...|>, or a RelationalDatabase / DatabaseReference.

tools.name: EntityPrefetch
tools.description: Downloads and caches the values of given properties for all entities of a class (or all properties of an entity) in one request, so subsequent EntityValue calls are served locally; essential for performance when looping over many entities, since each uncached EntityValue call is a network round trip. EntityValue with lists of entities and properties is the other batching technique.
tools.usage:
EntityPrefetch["type"]
EntityPrefetch[EntityClass["type", "class"]]
EntityPrefetch[class, {"prop1", "prop2"}]
EntityPrefetch[entity]
tools.example:
EntityPrefetch[EntityClass["Country", "Europe"], {"Population", "Area", "GDP"}];
Table[{CommonName[c], c["Population"]}, {c, EntityList[EntityClass["Country", "Europe"]]}] (* fast now *)

tools.name: RandomEntity
tools.description: Gives one or n random entities of a type or class, useful for sampling, testing and demos; FromEntity converts an entity to a related non-entity object (Molecule, Graph, Polyhedron, DateObject...) and ToEntity the reverse (e.g. a Molecule or chemical name to a Chemical entity, a GeoPosition to a City), and WolframLanguageData is the entity type describing Wolfram Language symbols themselves.
tools.usage:
RandomEntity["type"]
RandomEntity[class, n]
FromEntity[entity]
ToEntity[expr]
ToEntity[expr, "type"]
WolframLanguageData["Plot", "prop"]

tools.name: DatabaseReference
tools.description: Describes a connection to a SQL database (SQLite file, or MySQL/PostgreSQL/Oracle/SQL Server via association with "Backend", "Host", "Port", "Username", "Password", "Name") for RelationalDatabase (listed), which introspects the schema; EntityStore[RelationalDatabase[ref]] then exposes tables as entity types with EntityFunction filters compiled to SQL. This is the modern (12.0+) database path, distinct from the older DatabaseLink package.
tools.usage:
ref = DatabaseReference[File["db.sqlite"]]
ref = DatabaseReference[<|"Backend" -> "PostgreSQL", "Host" -> "localhost", "Port" -> 5432, "Name" -> "mydb", "Username" -> "u", "Password" -> "p"|>]
rdb = RelationalDatabase[ref]
rdb = RelationalDatabase[{"table1", "table2"}, ref]
EntityRegister[EntityStore[rdb]]
EntityValue["table1", {"col1", "col2"}, "Dataset"]

parameters.name: ref
parameters.description: File[...] for SQLite or an association of connection parameters.

tools.name: DatabaseConnect
tools.description: Opens (and DatabaseDisconnect closes) a persistent connection to the database behind a RelationalDatabase or its EntityStore, so that a sequence of queries reuses one connection instead of reconnecting per query; also useful to keep transactions or temporary tables alive. The connection is otherwise managed automatically.
tools.usage:
DatabaseConnect[rdb]
DatabaseConnect[store]
DatabaseDisconnect[rdb]

parameters.name: rdb
parameters.description: RelationalDatabase, EntityStore built on one, or entity type name.

tools.name: OpenSQLConnection
tools.description: DatabaseLink package (Needs["DatabaseLink`"]): OpenSQLConnection opens a JDBC connection (JDBC["driver", "host/db"] or a named connection from the DatabaseResources folder) returning an SQLConnection; SQLExecute (listed) runs raw SQL, while SQLSelect, SQLInsert, SQLUpdate, SQLDelete, SQLCreateTable and SQLDropTable build statements from Wolfram arguments; SQLTables / SQLColumns introspect the schema, CloseSQLConnection closes. JDBCDrivers lists bundled drivers (SQLite, MySQL, PostgreSQL, HSQLDB, H2...).
tools.usage:
Needs["DatabaseLink`"]
conn = OpenSQLConnection[JDBC["SQLite", "db.sqlite"]]
conn = OpenSQLConnection[JDBC["MySQL(Connector/J)", "host:3306/db"], "Username" -> "u", "Password" -> "p"]
SQLSelect[conn, "table", {"col1", "col2"}, SQLColumn["col1"] > 10]
SQLInsert[conn, "table", {"col1", "col2"}, {{1, "a"}, {2, "b"}}]
SQLExecute[conn, "SELECT * FROM t WHERE x > ?", {10}]
SQLTables[conn]
SQLColumns[conn, "table"]
CloseSQLConnection[conn]
JDBCDrivers[]
tools.notes: Package functions (DatabaseLink`), not System symbols; for schema-level work and entity queries prefer RelationalDatabase.

tools.name: MongoConnect
tools.description: MongoLink: MongoConnect opens a connection to a MongoDB server (returning a MongoClient object), MongoGetDatabase / MongoGetCollection select a collection, and MongoCollectionFind, MongoCollectionInsert, MongoCollectionUpdate, MongoCollectionAggregate perform document operations with Wolfram associations as BSON documents. The paclet loads automatically on first use.
tools.usage:
client = MongoConnect[]
client = MongoConnect["mongodb://user:pass@host:27017"]
coll = MongoGetCollection[client, "db", "collection"]
MongoCollectionInsert[coll, <|"name" -> "a", "x" -> 1|>]
MongoCollectionFind[coll, <|"x" -> <|"$gt" -> 0|>|>]
MongoCollectionCount[coll]
tools.notes: Requires a MongoDB server; function names are those of the MongoLink paclet as documented under reference.wolfram.com/language/MongoLink.

tools.name: RDFStore
tools.description: Semantic-web support: RDFStore[{RDFTriple[s, p, o], ...}] represents an RDF graph (also importable from Turtle/N-Triples/JSON-LD files and SPARQL endpoints), SPARQLExecute runs SPARQL queries (strings or symbolic SPARQLSelect / SPARQLConstruct forms) against a store or endpoint URL, and IRI represents internationalized resource identifiers. Use them to query Wikidata, DBpedia and internal knowledge graphs.
tools.usage:
store = RDFStore[{RDFTriple[IRI["http://ex.org/a"], IRI["http://ex.org/knows"], IRI["http://ex.org/b"]]}]
store = Import["data.ttl", "Turtle"]
SPARQLExecute[store, "SELECT ?s WHERE { ?s <http://ex.org/knows> ?o }"]
SPARQLExecute["https://query.wikidata.org/sparql", query]
SPARQLExecute[store, SPARQLSelect[RDFTriple[SPARQLVariable["s"], IRI["http://ex.org/knows"], SPARQLVariable["o"]]]]

parameters.name: query
parameters.description: SPARQL query string or symbolic query.

tools.example: SPARQLExecute["https://query.wikidata.org/sparql", "SELECT ?item ?itemLabel WHERE { ?item wdt:P31 wd:Q146 . SERVICE wikibase:label { bd:serviceParam wikibase:language \"en\" } } LIMIT 5"]
tools.notes: Provided by an auto-loading paclet (RDF/SPARQL functionality, 12.0+).

tools.name: SemanticInterpretation
tools.description: Interprets a natural-language string as a Wolfram Language expression using the same engine as free-form input (Ctrl+=), optionally restricted to a type or returning several candidates with AmbiguityFunction/AmbiguityList; Interpreter (listed) is the typed, form-oriented interface. Use SemanticInterpretation when the target type is unknown ("population of France in 1990" -> an EntityValue expression).
tools.usage:
SemanticInterpretation["text"]
SemanticInterpretation["text", form]
SemanticInterpretation["text", Hold]
SemanticInterpretation["text", AmbiguityFunction -> All]

parameters.name: form
parameters.description: Hold / HoldForm to see the expression unevaluated.

tools.example:
SemanticInterpretation["GDP of Germany", Hold]
SemanticInterpretation["three kilometers in miles"]

tools.name: Restricted
tools.description: Interpreter type modifiers used in Interpreter, APIFunction, FormFunction and Ask: Restricted["type", spec] limits values to a range, list or pattern; DelimitedSequence (listed) parses delimited lists; RepeatingElement and CompoundElement build form fields with repeated or grouped sub-fields; AnySubset offers multiple choice; GeoVariant selects location interpretation variants. They make user input validation declarative.
tools.usage:
Interpreter[Restricted["Integer", {1, 10}]]["7"]
Interpreter[Restricted["String", RegularExpression["[a-z]+"]]]["abc"]
Restricted["Number", {0, 1}]
Restricted["Country", EntityClass["Country", "Europe"]]
RepeatingElement["Integer"]
CompoundElement[{"x" -> "Number", "y" -> "Number"}]
AnySubset[{"a", "b", "c"}]

parameters.name: spec
parameters.description: {min, max}, list of allowed values, pattern, EntityClass, or predicate.

tools.name: SemanticImportString
tools.description: Applies SemanticImport's type inference (quantities, dates, entities, numbers) to a string containing CSV/TSV/table text instead of a file, returning a Dataset; options ExcludedLines, HeaderLines, Delimiters and MissingDataMethod ("Interpolate", "Nearest", value...) control parsing, and the second argument can specify column interpreters explicitly. Useful for data pasted from web pages or received over HTTP.
tools.usage:
SemanticImportString["csv text"]
SemanticImportString[text, {"String", "Number", "Date"}]
SemanticImportString[text, <|"col" -> "Quantity"|>]
SemanticImportString[text, Automatic, "Rows"]
SemanticImport[file, spec, HeaderLines -> 1, MissingDataMethod -> 0]

parameters.name: spec
parameters.description: List or association of Interpreter types per column, or Automatic.

tools.name: AmbiguityFunction
tools.description: Option of Interpreter, SemanticInterpretation and Ask controlling what happens when input is ambiguous: Automatic picks the best interpretation, All returns an AmbiguityList of candidates, or a custom function chooses. Interpreter (listed) shares a large catalogue of type names with APIFunction/FormFunction/Ask: numeric ("Integer", "Real", "Number", "Quantity"), text ("String", "Boolean", "Expression", "MathExpression"), dates ("Date", "Time", "DateTime"), knowledge ("Country", "City", "Person", "Chemical", any entity type), locations ("Location", "GeoCoordinates", "StreetAddress"), files ("Image", "Audio", "UploadedFile", "CloudObject"), web ("URL", "EmailAddress", "IPAddress", "Color") and "SemanticNumber"/"SemanticExpression" for free-form input.
tools.usage:
Interpreter["City", AmbiguityFunction -> All]["Springfield"]
Interpreter["Integer"]["42"]
Interpreter["Quantity"]["3 km/h"]
Interpreter["Country" | "City"]["Paris"]
Interpreter[{"Integer", "Real"}][{"1", "2.5"}]
tools.example:
Interpreter["City", AmbiguityFunction -> All]["Springfield"] (* AmbiguityList of candidate cities *)
Interpreter["EmailAddress"]["user@example.com"]
Interpreter["SemanticNumber"]["three thousand"]

tools.name: Dated
tools.description: Dated[entity, date] (or Dated["prop", date]) qualifies an entity or property with a date so that EntityValue returns historical values (population in 1950, a company's revenue in a given year). Related retrieval controls: EntityValue's third argument selects the output structure - "Association", "Dataset", "EntityAssociation", "PropertyAssociation", "EntityPropertyAssociation", "NonMissingEntities" - which is the key to getting tabular results from curated data in one call, and entity["prop"] / class["prop"] are shorthand for EntityValue.
tools.usage:
Dated[entity, date]
Dated["prop", date]
EntityValue[Dated[Entity["Country", "Germany"], 1950], "Population"]
EntityValue[class, {"p1", "p2"}, "Dataset"]
EntityValue[class, "prop", "EntityAssociation"]
EntityValue[entity, {"p1", "p2"}, "PropertyAssociation"]

tools.name: FormulaData
tools.description: Gives the equations of a named physical or mathematical formula (thousands are curated: "OhmsLaw", "IdealGasLaw", "KeplersThirdLaw", ...), solves them for unknowns when values are supplied, and returns properties such as "VariableDescriptions" and "QuantityVariableTable"; FormulaLookup searches formula names by keyword. Use them to pull standard formulas with units into calculations.
tools.usage:
FormulaData["name"]
FormulaData["name", {var1 -> q1, var2 -> q2}]
FormulaData["name", "prop"]
FormulaLookup["keyword"]
FormulaLookup["keyword", n]

parameters.name: {var -> q, ...}
parameters.description: Known quantities; the remaining variable is solved for.

tools.name: IsotopeData
tools.description: Curated physics data functions: IsotopeData (half-lives, masses, decay modes by {Z, A} or name), ParticleData (subatomic particle properties by name and charge), ThermodynamicData (fluid properties such as enthalpy or density as functions of temperature and pressure). They complement ElementData and ChemicalData (listed) for nuclear, particle and thermophysical calculations.
tools.usage:
IsotopeData[{Z, A}, "prop"]
IsotopeData["Uranium235", "HalfLife"]
IsotopeData["Carbon"] (* all isotopes *)
ParticleData["Proton", "Mass"]
ParticleData[{"Pion", 1}, "Lifetime"]
ThermodynamicData["Water", "Density", {"Temperature" -> Quantity[350, "Kelvins"], "Pressure" -> Quantity[2, "Atmospheres"]}]

tools.name: StarData
tools.description: Astronomy entity-data functions beyond AstronomicalData/PlanetData (listed): StarData, ExoplanetData and GalaxyData give properties (distance, magnitude, mass, coordinates) of catalogued objects, with the usual EntityClass and property-list forms; SolarSystemFeatureData, CometData, MinorPlanetData, SupernovaData and SatelliteData cover other object types. All return Quantities and Entities usable with AstroPosition/AstroGraphics.
tools.usage:
StarData["Sirius", "Distance"]
StarData[EntityClass["Star", "BrightStars"], {"Name", "ApparentMagnitude"}]
ExoplanetData["Kepler-22b", "OrbitalPeriod"]
GalaxyData["AndromedaGalaxy", "Distance"]
StarData["Properties"]

tools.name: EarthquakeData
tools.description: Retrieves earthquake events near a location (or worldwide) filtered by magnitude range and date interval, as a list of associations or a TimeSeries ("Magnitude", "Position", "Depth"), from the USGS-derived curated feed; suitable for GeoListPlot/GeoHistogram visualisations and seismic statistics.
tools.usage:
EarthquakeData[loc]
EarthquakeData[loc, {mmin, mmax}]
EarthquakeData[loc, {mmin, mmax}, {date1, date2}]
EarthquakeData[loc, {mmin, mmax}, {date1, date2}, "prop"]
EarthquakeData[All, {7, 10}, {DateObject[{2020, 1, 1}], Now}]

tools.name: MountainData
tools.description: Geographic feature data functions with the common entity-data signature: MountainData, LakeData, OceanData, IslandData, VolcanoData, GlacierData, DesertData, ParkData and related types give elevation, area, position, country and other properties for named features; each also works with EntityClass specifications and returns GeoPositions usable in GeoGraphics.
tools.usage:
MountainData["MountEverest", "Elevation"]
MountainData[EntityClass["Mountain", "EightThousanders"], {"Name", "Elevation"}]
LakeData["LakeBaikal", {"Area", "MaximumDepth"}]
OceanData["PacificOcean", "Area"]
MountainData["Properties"]

tools.name: AirportData
tools.description: Infrastructure and place data functions: AirportData (codes, positions, runways), BuildingData, BridgeData, TunnelData, DamData, NuclearReactorData, UniversityData and HistoricalSiteData, all following the entity-data calling pattern and returning quantities, positions and entities. Handy sources for logistics, geography and civil-engineering examples.
tools.usage:
AirportData["KLAX", "Position"]
AirportData[EntityClass["Airport", "Busiest"], {"Name", "Passengers"}]
BuildingData["BurjKhalifa", "Height"]
BridgeData["GoldenGateBridge", "MainSpan"]
UniversityData["MIT", "Enrollment"]

tools.name: CompanyData
tools.description: Socio-economic and cultural entity data: CompanyData (revenue, employees, ticker), PersonData (birth dates, occupations, notable people), MovieData (cast, release, box office) and LanguageData (speakers, scripts, families), all sharing the entity-data signature and backed by the same knowledge base as WolframAlpha; other types (e.g. "Book", "Artwork", "HistoricalEvent") are reached through Entity/EntityValue directly.
tools.usage:
CompanyData["Apple", "Revenue"]
CompanyData[EntityClass["Company", "Fortune500"], {"Name", "Employees"}]
PersonData["AlbertEinstein", "BirthDate"]
MovieData["Casablanca", "Cast"]
LanguageData["Japanese", "WritingSystems"]
tools.notes: Property availability varies by entity; use EntityValue[e, "Properties"] or the "Properties" argument to discover what is curated.

tools.name: AnatomyData
tools.description: Life-science entity data: AnatomyData gives properties and 3D models of anatomical structures (used with AnatomyPlot3D), PhysicalSystemData describes classical physical systems (equations, parameters), MedicalTestData describes lab tests with reference ranges; together with GenomeData/ProteinData (listed) and PlantData/SpeciesData they cover biomedical curated data.
tools.usage:
AnatomyData["Heart", "Mass"]
AnatomyData[Entity["AnatomicalStructure", "LeftLung"], "Graphics3D"]
AnatomyPlot3D[Entity["AnatomicalStructure", "Skull"]]
PhysicalSystemData["SimplePendulum", "Equations"]
MedicalTestData["BloodGlucose", "ReferenceRange"]

tools.name: ResourceSearch
tools.description: Searches the Wolfram Resource System (Function Repository, Data Repository, Neural Net Repository, Paclet Repository) for resources matching text, returning a Dataset of ResourceObjects with names, descriptions and types; the found objects are used with ResourceFunction/ResourceData/NetModel (listed). Use it to discover community functions and datasets programmatically.
tools.usage:
ResourceSearch["text"]
ResourceSearch["text", n]
ResourceSearch[{"text", "ResourceType" -> "DataResource"}]
ResourceSearch["text", "Names"]
ResourceSearch["text", "Objects"]

tools.name: DefineResourceFunction
tools.description: Turns a function definition into a ResourceFunction-style object with metadata (name, description, usage, examples) that can be used locally, registered by name with ResourceRegister, deployed to the cloud or submitted to the Wolfram Function Repository with ResourceSubmit; ResourceUpdate refreshes cached resources and ResourceRemove deletes local copies. This is the workflow for packaging and sharing single functions.
tools.usage:
rf = DefineResourceFunction[f]
rf = DefineResourceFunction[Function[x, x^2], "MySquare"]
rf = DefineResourceFunction[<|"Name" -> "MySquare", "Function" -> (#^2 &), "Description" -> "...", "Usage" -> ..., "Examples" -> ...|>]
ResourceRegister[rf]
ResourceRegister[rf, "Cloud"]
ResourceSubmit[rf]
ResourceUpdate["MySquare"]
ResourceRemove[rf]

parameters.name: f
parameters.description: Function or association of resource metadata.

tools.name: $ResourceSystemBase
tools.description: Base URL of the Wolfram Resource System used by ResourceObject, ResourceFunction, ResourceData, ResourceSearch and NetModel; ResourceSystemBase is the corresponding option for pointing individual calls at an alternative (e.g. Enterprise Private Cloud) resource system. Resources are cached locally after first download (ResourceRemove clears them).
tools.usage:
$ResourceSystemBase
$ResourceSystemBase = "https://cloud.mycompany.com/obj/resourcesystem/api/1.0"
ResourceObject["name", ResourceSystemBase -> url]

tools.name: DeviceOpen
tools.description: Opens a connection to a hardware device of a given class ("Serial", "Camera", "Arduino", "RaspberryPi", "GPIO", "Demo"...) returning a DeviceObject; DeviceConfigure sets parameters, DeviceClose releases it, and Devices / FindDevices list registered and detected devices. The Device Framework gives instruments, sensors and boards a uniform read/write/execute interface.
tools.usage:
dev = DeviceOpen["Serial", {"COM3", "BaudRate" -> 115200}]
dev = DeviceOpen["Camera"]
dev = DeviceOpen["Arduino", "COM4"]
DeviceConfigure[dev, "prop" -> value]
DeviceClose[dev]
Devices[]
FindDevices["Serial"]
DeviceObject[...]
tools.notes: Serial and camera drivers are built in; Arduino/Raspberry Pi/other drivers are installed as paclets.

tools.name: DeviceRead
tools.description: Reads the default item or named parameters from an open device (DeviceReadBuffer reads accumulated bytes, DeviceReadTimeSeries samples repeatedly into a TimeSeries, DeviceReadList reads n items), DeviceWrite sends values or parameter settings, and DeviceExecute runs device-specific commands (e.g. "Sketch" upload for Arduino, "Move" for a stage). These are the I/O verbs of the Device Framework used in lab automation.
tools.usage:
DeviceRead[dev]
DeviceRead[dev, "param"]
DeviceReadBuffer[dev]
DeviceReadTimeSeries[dev, {dt, ttotal}]
DeviceReadTimeSeries[dev, {dt, ttotal}, "param"]
DeviceWrite[dev, value]
DeviceWrite[dev, {"param" -> value}]
DeviceExecute[dev, "command", params]
DeviceStreams[dev]
